title: Quick fixes — session fade, project switcher, games

steps.headline: Sessions menu: the see-through fade — keep?
steps.changed: The list's top and bottom edges now fade to clear, the same fade as popups and Resume. It used to paint a band of the menu's colour over the last row.
steps.notice: Look at the last row (llama) on Meadow Mist: before, a pale band covers it; after, the row fades into the glass. On solid themes (Light, Midnight) the two look almost the same, which is expected.

steps.headline: Project switcher: ✕, no check mark, softer rows — keep?
steps.changed: The "esc" chip is now the usual ✕ (Esc still closes it). The current project no longer has a check mark or an outlined box: rows now look like the sessions menu, with a stronger tint on the row under your mouse or arrow keys and a light tint on the current project. The two full-width lines are now the short faded dividers popups use.
steps.notice: When it opens, your current project is also the highlighted row, so it shows the stronger tint until you move. There's still no way to remove a synced project; that's on the redesign list, not in this batch.

steps.headline: Games list: standard cards — keep?
steps.changed: The four game tiles and the sign-in note are now the app's standard first-level cards (outline, light fill), not darker boxes. The line under "Games" is now the short faded divider, and the ✕ is the shared one.
steps.notice: The sign-in note's "Sign in" is still a bare text link; the bare-text buttons batch will fix it with the others.

steps.headline: Games lobby: labelled cards instead of lines — keep?
steps.changed: The full-width lines are gone. Each part is now a small label with a card under it: Your profile, Add a friend, Friends (1). Each friend is a box inside the Friends card, 8px apart. A challenge or "declined" message now uses the standard notice box.
steps.notice: "Go Incognito" is still a bare text button and a failed friend request still shows red text; the bare-text and red-text batches cover those. The chat under a game in play keeps its lines, because the game screens are exempt.
